title: Parsing and normalising author names
text: Bibliometric exports use three incompatible conventions. parse_names() recognises three; rule decided per string. comma always means Last, First. comma-less strings surname_first argument controls interpretation: "auto" (default) — surname-first iff trailing token looks like initials (-uppercase, 1–3 letters). bibnets-takes-precedence bias: native bibnets/Scopus labels parse correctly extra arguments, ordinary mixed-case "First Last" never misread. "yes" / TRUE — force surname-first. "" / FALSE — force given-first (comma-less returned unchanged). Particles suffixes handled, detection case-insensitive works bibnets’ upper-cased labels: Group / corporate authors, NA, empty strings left untouched:
code: parse_names(c("Saqr, Mohammed", "WANG Y", "Mohammed Saqr")) #> [1] "Mohammed Saqr" "Y WANG"        "Mohammed Saqr" #> attr(,"parts") #>         original    first last particle suffix   type #> 1 Saqr, Mohammed Mohammed Saqr     <NA>   <NA> person #> 2         WANG Y        Y WANG     <NA>   <NA> person #> 3  Mohammed Saqr Mohammed Saqr     <NA>   <NA> person parse_names("Wang Yong", surname_first = "yes")   # force surname-first #> [1] "Yong Wang" #> attr(,"parts") #>    original first last particle suffix   type #> 1 Wang Yong  Yong Wang     <NA>   <NA> person parse_names("WANG Y",    surname_first = "no")    # force given-first #> [1] "WANG Y" #> attr(,"parts") #>   original first last particle suffix   type #> 1   WANG Y  WANG    Y     <NA>   <NA> person parse_names(c("van der Berg, Jan", "Smith, John, Jr.",               "DE LA CRUZ, ANA", "VAN DER BERG J")) #> [1] "Jan van der Berg" "John Smith Jr"    "ANA DE LA CRUZ"   "J VAN DER BERG"   #> attr(,"parts") #>            original first  last particle suffix   type #> 1 van der Berg, Jan   Jan  Berg  van der   <NA> person #> 2  Smith, John, Jr.  John Smith     <NA>     Jr person #> 3   DE LA CRUZ, ANA   ANA  CRUZ    DE LA   <NA> person #> 4    VAN DER BERG J     J  BERG  VAN DER   <NA> person parse_names(c("WHO Collaborating Group", NA, "")) #> [1] "WHO Collaborating Group" NA                        #> [3] ""                        #> attr(,"parts") #>                  original first last particle suffix         type #> 1 WHO Collaborating Group  <NA> <NA>     <NA>   <NA> organization #> 2                    <NA>  <NA> <NA>     <NA>   <NA>      missing #> 3                          <NA> <NA>     <NA>   <NA>        empty

title: bibnets 0.5.0
text: Custom data sets, column name, separator. Every network builder now takes self-describing column argument plus sep, non-standard CSV works single call without renaming columns pre-splitting strings: author_network(d, authors = "Author Names", sep = ",") keyword_network(d, keywords = "Tags", sep = ",") reference_network(d, references = "Cited Refs", sep = ",") document_network(d, references = "Cited Refs", sep = ",") source_network(d, journal = "Source title") country_network(d, countries = "Nations", sep = ",") institution_network(d, affiliations = "Orgs", sep = ",") local_citations() historiograph() gain references + sep. sep accepts delimiter (",", "|", " ", …) applies named entity column. new arguments sit end signature, existing positional calls unaffected. references_sep — author_network(), country_network(), institution_network(), source_network() gain references_sep argument (default ";") references column used coupling can separator, independent entity sep. (Reference strings often contain internal commas, separate.) strip_quotes — every builder gains strip_quotes argument (default TRUE) removes surrounding quote characters (straight ", doubled "", curly quotes) entity, quoted CSV value like "Alice" ""Alice"" treated Alice. Set strip_quotes = FALSE keep quotes part label. Applies freshly-split strings entities supplied list-column. parse_names(): optional, standalone utility reorders author names "First Last" parses first/last/particle/suffix components (attached "parts" attribute). Handles three conventions: "Last, First" (comma), Scopus / bibnets "SURNAME Initials" label form ("WANG Y", "AYALA-ROMERO JA"), "First Last". surname_first argument ("auto"/"yes"/"", default "auto") controls comma-less interpretation, auto-detection biased toward bibnets/Scopus convention native bibnets labels parse without extra arguments. Case-insensitive (recognises particles bibnets’ uppercased labels). format argument selects output style: "first_last" (default), "last_initials" ("Saqr M."), "last" ("Saqr"). Detects group/corporate authors leaves , NA, empty strings unchanged. called reader network builder — entity labels still matched verbatim unless apply . Base R ; new dependencies. title: bibnets 0.3.0
